problem: Existing embodied systems treat tool/API/IoT invocation and physical manipulation as separate pipelines, linearly concatenate interaction history (context blow-up, lost or conflicting information), and rely on open-loop VLA policies that cannot detect or recover from physical failures.
motivation: Everyday physical autonomy needs coordinating heterogeneous cyber-physical tools within a single task flow and recovering from failures over long horizons. The authors argue this calls for a hierarchical asynchronous architecture that separates planning, long-horizon state tracking and real-time verification, rather than one monolithic end-to-end model.
key_idea: OmniAct pairs a skill-routing VLM planner over a unified cyber-physical action space with event-boundary-compressed hierarchical memory (sensory/episodic/reflective) and an asynchronous VLM visual monitor that preempts execution and triggers replanning on anomalies.
insight: Adding reflective memory on top of episodic compression raises constraint satisfaction over the best ablation variant by 13-20 points (e.g. Tool Use 86.67% vs 56.67%). Sliding Window collapses to 6.67-13.33%, and Raw History only reaches 46.67-66.67% despite full information. Compression alone trades dilution for information loss, and explicit long-term constraint retrieval is what matters. The framework also lifts Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B from 50.0% to 80.0% without training, but gains vanish for the 8B model (+6.7), which struggles to emit well-formed structured outputs.
method: Unified skill-routing action space: each action a_t=(tau_t, g_t) selects a skill (VLA pick_and_place, navigate_to, IoT control, web/API query, speak, get_observation) with parameters; a_t ~ pi(.|c_t,H_t,T)
Multimodal semantic planner: a VLM (Gemini-3.1-Pro by default) interprets speech/vision/state, decomposes tasks and emits structured JSON with one next step (parallel dispatch supported)

Asynchronous visual preemption: a separate VLM monitor, given only before/during/after images with no task context, periodically checks execution; on anomaly it halts the VLA and returns the failure context for replanning (default monitor Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B)
Sensory memory: FIFO queue of recent frames for the control policy and monitor, decoupled from planner context
Episodic memory: timestamped event-boundary-driven compression of raw observation sequences into keyframe summaries, giving sub-linear context growth
Reflective memory: stores static priors (tool schemas, skills) and failure reflections (root cause and corrective strategy) plus long-term preferences, retrieved and injected at planning time

Low-level executors: self-trained pi0-style VLA fine-tuned on in-house teleoperation data for manipulation; classical waypoint following on a pre-built 2D semantic map for navigation; deterministic HTTP calls for cyber skills

setting.backbone: Gemini-3.1-Pro (frozen planner); Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B (frozen visual monitor); self-trained pi0-style VLA for manipulation
setting.training_data: Planner and monitor are training-free (prompted). Only the pi0-style VLA low-level policy is fine-tuned on in-house teleoperation data (scale not given).
setting.observation: RGB frames (two third-person + wrist camera on UR5e; RGB on mobile robot), speech transcripts, IoT/API state
setting.action_space: Discrete skill calls with parameters (pick_and_place, navigate_to to semantic locations, IoT control, web/API queries, speak, get_observation)
setting.privileged: Pre-built 2D semantic map of the indoor environment for navigation; otherwise none

numbers_note: Not a standard navigation benchmark. The main per-level E2E/Sub results (L1, L2, overall) are only in a figure, so only L3 numbers quoted in the text are captured. No standard benchmarks (R2R, ObjectNav, etc.) reported.
results: On 40 real-world tasks (UR5e and Keenon), OmniAct reaches L3 E2E of 50.0% (manipulation) and 54.2% (navigation), beating the best baselines (SayCan 43.8%, Code as Policy 37.5%), with L3 Sub of 80.5%/80.6% vs best baseline 60.9%/57.9%. Memory keeps per-call tokens at about 4k-8k over 270 rounds, while raw history grows past 120k. Constraint satisfaction rises up to 86.67% and the framework improves all six backbones, most for Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B (+30.0).
limitations: The planner cannot improve the frozen VLA policies, so recovery is bounded by the existing skill repertoire
The visual monitor runs at VLM inference frequency, leaving a latency window with unchecked actions (safety risk for fragile objects or people nearby)

Small-scale evaluation (40 tasks, 20-sample verifier test, 10 samples per memory scenario) with human judging; navigation uses a pre-built semantic map and waypoint following; tiny 8B models give little benefit
